description: herdr's rules for runtime/github/arm.sh. herdr is a public fork of a Rust terminal multiplexer and the operator's console: it runs the operator's shell sessions, speaks a socket API, and ships binaries that users install by piping a script. boundary.paths: CI, release and deploy workflows and their owner lists (.github/), the git hooks (.githooks/), the dependency and build surface (Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock at any depth, build.rs, .cargo/, rust-toolchain.toml, clippy.toml, the Nix flake and nix/, justfile), every script that builds, releases, vendors, packages or tests an installer (scripts/, packaging/), the installers and the release manifests they download from (distribution/install.*, distribution/latest.json, distribution/preview.json), the vendored third-party code, which is supply surface (vendor/), the harness and editor wiring that can load code or instructions (.claude/, .mcp.json, .agents/, .pi/, .zed/), and words where the boundary is a file anywhere (secret, credential, token, auth, signing, trust, api key, private key). The bare word key is not on it: a terminal's keyboard handling is its product, not its trust. boundary.exempt is dropped first, but never under .github/, .claude/, .agents/ or .pi/ (a skill or a command file is what the harness runs, not prose): Markdown and MDX prose, the documentation tree docs/, and .agent-fabric/. No classes. waiver_role is null: only the owner waives the boundary.
